title: KV prefill strategy scrub - midweek notes
body:
Meeting: informal scrub (midweek)
Date: 2026-06-16
Attendees: Riley, Aarav, Elena, Samir, Nina (partial)
Goal: Triage the prefill + KV-cache tuning experiments, decide immediate roll-forward candidates, capture follow-ups for next sprint.

High-level summary
- Recent prefill heuristic (PR 1423) improves average token latency for warm sessions but shows a small P95 regression on cold starts when combined with the new microbatch window logic.
- Measured on the internal BERT-like seqgen workload: baseline P50=21ms P95=72ms, after prefill P50=14ms (-33%), P95=84ms (+17%) on cold-start-heavy traffic.
- KV-hit rate increased from 58% to 73% for steady-state conversational traces; however warmup sequences show increased memory pressure because prefill buffers multiple key shards at higher batch sizes.

What we tested (quick recap)
- Prefill-size tuning: tried prefill-lengths [8, 16, 32] with adaptive eviction. 16 provided the best steady-state hit/latency tradeoff.
- Cold warmup guard: a conservative path that disables aggressive prefill for sessions with <2 prior requests. Reduced P95 regression but also reduced overall hit gains.
- Batch-window interplay: microbatch window of 8ms vs 16ms interacts with prefill because larger windows accumulate more KV entries per request, increasing transient memory.
- Kernel-level mem alloc: observed increased fragmentation on quantized kernels (int8) when prefill populates large contiguous KV vectors; suspected allocator pattern in kernels/alloc.cc.

Measurements (testbed: ded-qa-gpu-8, repeated 30 runs each)
- Baseline (no prefill): P50 21ms, P95 72ms, throughput 110 req/s, kv-hit 58%
- Prefill len=16 + microbatch 8ms: P50 14ms, P95 84ms, throughput 125 req/s, kv-hit 73%
- Prefill len=8 + microbatch 8ms + cold-guard: P50 16ms, P95 75ms, throughput 120 req/s, kv-hit 68%
- Observed 2x increase in transient peak RSS during warmup for len=16 runs.

Risks / notes
- Memory fragmentation on quantized paths can cause OOMs in worst-case when multiple large sessions prefill simultaneously on the same device.
- The cold-start P95 regression is user-visible for low-frequency interactive flows; must avoid regressions for hosted customers with strict latency SLOs.
- Rollout plan should be region-limited and use canary traffic with fallback to baseline model variant.

Decisions made
- Do NOT roll prefill len=16 cluster-wide yet. We will iterate on a hybrid: enable len=16 for dedicated pools with >64GB memory per GPU, and keep conservative len=8 + cold-guard for hosted shared pools.
- Merge kernel allocator probe first (small PR to add heap-snapshot logging) to better understand fragmentation before touching kernel alloc strategy.
- Add an A/B test in canary for dedicated pools to measure user-impact over a 48h window.

Action items
- Samir: open an issue in runtime repo capturing allocator fragmentation traces, attach heap-snapshots from the failing runs. Due: 2026-06-18. Linked: github PR 1423 (mentioned above).
- Aarav: implement cold-guard toggle in config (runtime flag) + document config in console rollout page. Due: 2026-06-19. Linked artifact: Jira INF-987.
- Elena: run long-duration soak (72h) on two dedicated pools with prefill len=16 and report memory/latency deltas. Start: 2026-06-17, report: 2026-06-20.
- Nina: update canary rollout playbook with explicit fallback thresholds (P95 increase >10% or OOM incidence >0.1%). Due: 2026-06-18.
- Riley: schedule kernel probe merge and coordinate with SRE for temporary increased logs on ded-qa-gpu-8. Due: 2026-06-17.

Open questions / brainstorm
- Can we compress prefilled KV shards in-place (LZ4) to reduce RSS without slowing hot-path? Will need microbench of compress/decompress latency inside kernel hot path.
- Alternative: lazy prefill where we only prefetch top-K heads likely to be hit (predictive prefetch from recent token distribution). Need an inexpensive prediction routine.
- How aggressive should eviction be when memory pressure is detected? Immediate LRU vs weighted TTL-based eviction tied to request age?

Notes to file (informal)
- Tweets from infra: observed a spike in Slack alerts at 03:12 UTC for OOM on quantized bundles; exact run ids in logs: run-6643, run-6644.
- Useful traces: /var/log/runtime/alloc-snapshots/2026-06-16-03*.tgz (SRE has access).

Next sync
- Quick sync Friday 09:30am PT: short rollup after Elena's soak and Samir's allocator issue details. Expect to decide on canary start Monday.

Attachments (for context)
- experiment run csvs (internal): gs://redwood-qa/prefill/2026-06-16/summary.csv
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1423
- Jira: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-987

End of notes.
